claims.text: Conventionally produced powder-bed additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components exhibit dimensional inaccuracies.
Conventionally produced powder-bed additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components exhibit porosity.
Conventionally produced powder-bed additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components exhibit residual-stress-induced microcracking.
An in-situ laser re-melting pass after every deposited layer will refine the alloy microstructure.
An in-situ laser re-melting pass after every deposited layer will make the microstructure more homogeneous.
An in-situ laser re-melting pass after every deposited layer will reduce porosity.
An in-situ laser re-melting pass after every deposited layer will lower residual stresses.
Locally re-melting freshly deposited material promotes homogenization.
Locally re-melting freshly deposited material reduces thermal gradients.
Reduced thermal gradients from re-melting reduce residual stresses.
Layerwise laser re-melting allows pores to heal before solidification.
Layerwise laser re-melting allows microcracks to heal before solidification.
Layerwise laser re-melting will improve dimensional accuracy relative to conventional powder-bed fusion without re-melting.
Layerwise laser re-melting will reduce fabrication-induced defects relative to conventional powder-bed fusion without re-melting.
Layerwise laser re-melting will increase tensile strength relative to conventional powder-bed fusion without re-melting.
Layerwise laser re-melting will increase ductility relative to conventional powder-bed fusion without re-melting.
The predicted improvement should hold under typical build-plate temperatures, inert atmosphere, and typical laser parameters.
The magnitude of improvement depends on the alloy's thermal properties and composition.
The magnitude of improvement depends on the specific re-melting and additive-manufacturing process parameters.
